headline: High: B’s broad network/MCP/browser access can amplify A’s untrusted content into prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A is a content-writing repo with no runtime surfaces, so it cannot inject by itself; however B uses MCP, browsers, and natural-language commands, and could ingest A-produced text or diagrams as instructions if bridged through files or copy-paste. The interaction is plausible but undocumented, so uncertainty pushes above low.
conditions: IF A-generated text is pasted into B's command channel or imported as a file that B parses as instructions, injection becomes reachable.
IF B is configured to treat document content as authoritative prompts, attacker-controlled content can steer tool use.
mitigations: Disable automatic prompt ingestion from imported files.
Require explicit provenance labels on all A-produced content.
Use a read-only staging folder for imports.
Add a manual review step before B executes any instruction-like text.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance tracking in B.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no I/O surfaces, but B handles files, broad network egress, and API keys. If A’s outputs include sensitive material and are fed into B, B can transmit that context to third-party APIs. The pairwise leak path is indirect yet realistic in default document-processing workflows.
conditions: IF sensitive text from A is imported into B, B may forward it to external model APIs.
IF B is run with API keys present in environment variables, leaked context can accompany outbound requests.
mitigations: Remove secrets from B’s runtime environment.
Restrict B to local-only models for sensitive inputs.
Redact sensitive fields before import.
Use a separate workspace for A outputs and B inputs.
requires-engineering: enforce egress allowlists and secret-scoped execution.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write, network, or concurrency surfaces, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. B supports multiple instances and broad network access, but without any overlapping writable surface from A there is no meaningful write-write conflict. The only plausible overlap is manual handoff, which is small and non-destructive.
conditions: IF both agents are manually pointed at the same mutable directory, file clobbering becomes possible.
IF B instances are run concurrently on the same workspace without locking, conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent.
Avoid concurrent B instances on the same files.
Turn on filesystem backups or versioning.
Keep A as a non-writing reference source.
requires-engineering: add workspace locking to B.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a repository of prompt-engineering material, so its outputs can be treated as guidance; B uses natural-language commands and AI-assisted visualization, making it likely to act on imported instructions without strong verification. That creates a plausible cascade where A’s content becomes B’s operational input. The interaction is inferred, not directly evidenced, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF B consumes A-derived text as an instruction source, B may execute or render incorrect actions.
IF B lacks a verification gate for imported prompts, errors from A can propagate downstream.
mitigations: Require citations for any A-derived claim before B acts on it.
Use a human approval step for generated diagrams or actions.
Separate reference material from executable instructions.
Limit B to draft-only mode for imported content.
requires-engineering: add verification and provenance checks before action-taking.

E_compliance.rationale: A is open-source documentation with no touched data classes, while B explicitly handles API keys and can send files to external AI providers across multiple vendors. Even without a named residency mismatch, B’s broad egress and secret handling create a compliance gap if regulated or sensitive content from A is processed. A is not the compliance driver; B is.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into B, outbound calls to third-party APIs may violate policy.
IF API keys are stored in B’s environment, retention/logging controls must cover them.
mitigations: Do not process regulated data in B.
Use local models for sensitive workflows.
Rotate and scope API keys narrowly.
Review vendor retention settings before use.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls for each API provider.
